newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian palm oil ends down on technical play.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian palm oil ends down on technical play.

text.p: Malaysian palm oil prices ended lower on technical play after a lack of positive statistics and overseas interest left the market void of leads, dealers said.
A new support of around 1,180 ringgit was called after the support level of 1,200 was broken in early trade, said dealers.
They said main activity for the day was switching of nearby positions to forwards.
"There was also September/October covering by refineries," said a trader.
Prices opened under a bearish gloom with the Chicago soyoil futures closed on Monday for holiday, and local traders still disputing freshly-issued export estimates for May 1-25.

Cargo surveyor Societe Generale de Surveillance (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd on Monday estimated export for the first 25 days of May at 547,382 tonnes, against the 549,976 tonnes recorded for April 1-25. Traders said the estimate was too high.
With little leads to go on, the market, however, pulled back earlier losses through technical play, said traders.
"From here, I would put support (for August third-month) at 1,180 and resistance at 1,250," said one trader.
At the close, the August futures contract closed six ringgit down at 1,200 ringgit ($477.23) a tonne after falling to a low of 1,195 ringgit earlier.
Volume on the futures market was at 2,576 lots.
Physicals followed futures, with interest confined to nearby months, said traders.

May (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,270 ringgit against bids of 1,265 after trading at 1,265. May (central) was offered at 1,260 against bids of 1,255, with earlier trades of 1,260 and 1,255. June (south) saw offers at 1,270 against bids at 1,265 after trading at 1,265.
In refined products, June RBD palm oil was offered at $535, July at $530, Aug/Sept at $525.
June RBD palm olein saw offers at $572.50, July at 565, and Aug/Sept at $555. June was traded at $570, while July/Aug/Sept was done at $555.
June RBD palm stearin was offered at $405 and June/July palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $270.
